title: Digital Twins Explained: Test a Change Before Making It
headline:
Test the change
before the real world.
meaning: A digital twin represents a real system.
example: Try a factory-layout change in a connected simulation.
comparison: A useful twin connects its model to relevant real-world data.
caution: Simulation results depend on model and data quality.
question: What would you test in a digital twin?
lines: What if you could test a factory change before moving a single machine? That is one use of digital twins.
A digital twin is a digital representation of a real object or system, connected to relevant data.
A team might simulate a different layout and inspect how people, machines, or materials move.
The point is not just a beautiful three dimensional picture. The connection to the real system makes it useful.
A simulation is only as dependable as its assumptions, model, and data. Check those before acting.
